designFindings: Endless verification loop. An apply refusal that is not a conflict ends nothing: no finish runs and no incident is logged, and the lease stays `verifying`. recover reschedules it every 10 minutes, and the same refusal comes back each time, forever. Evidence: verify.ts:155-158 ignores applied.outcome; attempts.ts:109, :122-126, :142-143; evidence.ts:203-206; recoveries.ts:40-49.

Two settlement paths with different rules and side effects. The receipt path (sends.ts:46-64, :185-244) checks documentHash, userOpHash and chainId. It also writes a commitmentEvidence row, a paymentEvidenceConflicts row on mismatch, a Documents Memo (evidence.ts:91) and the Request's registered receipt (evidence.ts:115). The indexed path (settlements.ts:84-157, settlement-facts.ts:44-55) checks only router, settlement id, sender, recipient, token, amount and kind, and writes none of these. When the index wins the race (the D2 intent), the receipt item becomes a replay (replays.ts:19-37), so the Memo and Request receipt are never written by this area. A later reorg correction also finds no consumed row to reverse (history.ts:179-207).

Silent rail-payout miscount. applyRailDeliveryInTx answers `replayed` while Banking's delivery is pending (rails.ts:33-39), even though the caller just moved the Payment from settling to in_transit (sends.ts:223, settlements.ts:140). settle then counts it in no bucket, so open no longer equals settled + pending + refused (settle.ts:70-72), and apply reports the command `replayed` instead of `applied` (attempts.ts:162-166).

Guard works by accident. apply passes recordPaymentCommandOutcome the command document it read before patching `applied` (attempts.ts:111-161), so the `verificationState === 'applied'` guard in outcomes.ts:27 never fires on this path.

Two kinds of mismatch ending. A conflict quarantine (conflicts.ts:66-75) sets `mismatch` on whichever command owns the evidence's hash, whatever state it is in, and records no outcome, Payment change or Attempt change. finish-mismatch (finishes.ts:272-283) sets `mismatch` and records an `unresolved` outcome that moves settling Payments to unresolved and sent Attempts to unknown.

Telemetry writes domain rows. Every scheduled payment_transitioned or payment_verification_retry patches each Payment's lifecycleSequence, and its terminalOutcome, terminalEventId and terminalAt for a terminal event (events/writer.ts:187-222). The terminal claim on a Payment therefore lives in telemetry code, and a retry event writes every Payment of the command.

Settlement side effects copied five times, with differences. The payroll run settle, the Request's paid notice, the Books fact and the settled event are coded separately in sends.ts:226-243, settlements.ts:143-155, rails.ts:58-74, claims.ts:87-100 and commitments.ts:163-178. claims.ts books only the claim fact, without recordSettledPaymentInTx. The re-verification path books both the claim fact and the settled-payment fact and schedules no settled event. A completing claim is therefore booked differently on the first pass and on a re-verification.

Commands ended outside the outcome writer. voidLandedInTx and chainCancelledInTx set completionOutcome failed / lastExecutionOutcome superseded directly (voids.ts:99-107, board-cancels.ts:38-44) and cancel Payments through transitionPayment(voided) (voids.ts:112-117, board-cancels.ts:45-50). The voided command's Attempt and the Payments' executionOutcome are never updated, and a chain cancel emits no payment_transitioned for its cancelled Payments.

Settle scheduled where it cannot settle. finish-void classifies the void's Attempt succeeded, which schedules settle (voids.ts:72, lifecycles.ts:216), then cancels those same Payments in the same transaction (voids.ts:110-117). finish-budget-schedule schedules settle at reservation time (budget-schedules.ts:84), though Budgets pays on the date and the due job schedules it again (schedules/writes.ts:175).

`applied` means three different things: verified evidence settled the command (attempts.ts:145-161), a void landed with completionOutcome settled (voids.ts:73-80), and a Budgets reservation proved with no completion and no money moved (budget-schedules.ts:85-89).

Possible permanent block on settlement (plausible, not reproduced). If a Deposit rollback is refused, removeMovementProjection throws an invariant (overlays.ts:62-66), for example on a changed digest (rollbacks.ts:51-57). The whole settlement mutation fails on both paths, and the minute sweep retries the same Payment forever.

Budget schedule reads its receipt twice. readBudgetScheduleDecision reads it through readVoidDecision → readOperationEvidence (external.ts:217; executions/external/attempts.ts:71), then fetches the same receipt again for its logs (external.ts:222).

Circular dependency between Payments and Documents. evidence.ts:91 calls documents prepareMovementMemoInTx, which calls back into payments captureMemoConflictRemovalInTx (documents/writes/memos.ts:202 → payments/movements/writes/corrections.ts:29).

No limit on provider failures. provider_failure retries forever with no incident, and the backoff grows from verificationAttempt, not from any failure count (finishes.ts:78-80, :106-110). A provider outage keeps commands cycling between retry_wait and verifying with no terminal state.

Operator resumes have no surface. retry-mismatch and retry-unresolved are internal mutations that only tests call (verify.test.ts:1195, apply.test.ts:168); there is no CLI or role check. They also move any `unresolved` Payment, including a commitment held by history replay, to `settling`, which is a send status (recoveries.ts:139-141).

Decisions made on an unleased snapshot (plausible). verify reads the command context in a separate query before begin takes the lease (verify.ts:123 vs :126). The void, budget and pool decisions use that snapshot's activeExecutionId, userOpHash, sender and sponsorship (verify.ts:128-149).
Router address in the wrong module. paymentRouterInTx takes a collection's router address from the companies-house integration (reads/routers.ts:6, :31; integrations/companies-house/addresses.ts:58).

No door to neighbor concepts. Deep verification helpers import neighbor concepts' writers directly, and each settlement path wires its own set: sends.ts:5-10 (#banking, #books, #payroll, #requests), evidence.ts:7-8 (#requests, #documents), history.ts:8-10 (#books, #documents, #payroll), rails.ts:2-6. The verifications area also writes the movements area's tables (movements, movement-attributions, deposit-materializations, and the Deposit Payment row) through suppressSettledProtocolMovement (conflicts.ts:49-64, overlays.ts:43-67).
